guidanceConsulted.query: responsive reference documentation tables without horizontal overflow on mobile
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Lean on intrinsic sizing; wrap potentially-wide content in overflow containers; use overflow-wrap on unbreakable tokens; let flex rows wrap; prefer logical, content-driven sizing over fixed widths.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied: every data table sits in .table-wrap{overflow-x:auto}; overflow-wrap:anywhere on h1, lede, code and table cells (long Chromium source URLs and flag names are the overflow risk on these pages); baseline-browsers list uses flex-wrap; pre blocks scroll internally so 80-column quoted Chromium code never widens the page. Exception: no container queries — the shared single-column editorial measure fits the reference format, matching prior accepted pages.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible code blocks and long-line pre code overflow in technical documentation
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use native semantic structure (pre/code for code, tables with proper header cells, headings in order) and let the browser's defaults do interaction work; avoid clipping content invisibly.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied: all examples are semantic <pre><code> with HTML-escaped content; quoted C++/Rust/JSON5 kept verbatim inside code blocks rather than screenshots; doc-tables use th scope=row and thead; overflow is scroll (visible affordance), never clip; banners use role=note with aria-label instead of bare styled divs.
